title: Google Playground: Create browser games with AI prompts
key_facts: Google launched Playground on 7 Oct 2026, an experimental platform for creating, playing and sharing custom games.
Users describe a game in prompts and revise it through a conversational interface; genres include trivia and racing, in 2D or 3D.
Games run in browsers on phones and laptops; creators can keep them private, share links or publish to an Explore gallery.
An upcoming Unity Spark integration is promised.
Google says published games always go through safety screenings.
Initially available to US adults; creation access depends on Google AI subscriptions and uses weekly tokens, while playing is free.
Rivals include Roblox's prompt-based Build tool (announced July) and Rosebud AI; Google calls Playground an 'early experiment'.
quote_evidence: Google wants the next hit browser game to start with a prompt.
Playground is initially available to U.S. adults, with creation access rolling out based on Google AI subscriptions.
why_it_matters_hint: Anyone could make a simple browser game by describing it, if Google's tool works as described.
notes: Event on 7 Oct, before the 8 Oct window start, so lowered by 1. A Financial Times headline on the same launch also appears in Google News.
